newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soybeans, soymeal turn higher on funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soybeans, soymeal turn higher on funds.

text.p: CBOT July soybean and soymeal futures turned higher at midsession on heavy fund buying, shrugging off bearish data in USDA's crop report released early Tuesday, traders said.
"The funds dumped millions into this market and they weren't about to let the market turn against them," a floor trader said.
USDA on Tuesday left unchanged its estimate for 1996-97 ending soybean stocks. The figure stands at 140 million bushels.
The trade had expected USDA to shave 10 million to 15 million bushels off its ending stocks estimate.
Soyoil futures also turned around with the July and August contracts on the plus side.
Traders said Refco Inc and Rosenthal Collins each bought three million bushels May, Dean Witter, FIMAT Futures and Merrill Lynch each bought one million May and Cargill Inc bought one million May.

At 1025 CST, soybeans were 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 cents higher with May up 1/2 at $8.60-1/2 a bushel. Soymeal was $3.00 per ton lower to $0.40 higher with May up $0.10 at $275.80. Soyoil was down 0.17 cent per lb to up 0.03 with May down 0.07 at 26.26.
